pr.title: Return 404 when search yields no results

behavioralChanges.summary: search() now returns status 404 + error body when no documents match, instead of status 200 + empty results array.
behavioralChanges.after: search('zzz-no-match') → { status: 404, body: { error: 'No results found' } }

sources.note: New branch: if results.length === 0, return { status: 404, body: { error: 'No results found' } }.
SearchResponse type widened from a single { status: 200 } interface to a union: SearchResponseOk | SearchResponseNotFound.

behavioralChanges.summary: Blank and whitespace-only queries now also return 404, not 200 + empty list. The blank-query path was not explicitly covered in the PR description.
behavioralChanges.after: search('   ') → { status: 404, body: { error: 'No results found' } }

sources.note: Blank query still produces results = [] via the q.length === 0 early path, then falls into the same results.length === 0 branch that returns 404.
Existing test asserts body.results === [] for blank query — now fails because body has no 'results' key on a 404 response.

behavioralChanges.summary: searchClient.ts is not updated: interpretResponse() still accesses response.body.results unconditionally, which is a TypeScript type error and a runtime crash on any 404 response.
behavioralChanges.before: interpretResponse() assumed response.body always has a results array and branched on its length.
behavioralChanges.after: The service now returns a body with an error string (not a results array) on 404. interpretResponse() has not been updated — it will access .results on a 404 body, returning undefined at runtime.

sources.note: interpretResponse() reads response.body.results.length unconditionally. TypeScript now reports: Property 'results' does not exist on type '{ error: string }'.
JSDoc comment still describes the baseline 200-only assumption — the function was not updated as part of this change.

reviewLocations.label: searchClient.ts:24-29 — interpretResponse() not updated
reviewLocations.reason: This is the most critical gap: the service change is incomplete without a corresponding client update. interpretResponse() accesses response.body.results unconditionally and will crash at runtime on a 404 response. TypeScript already flags this as a type error on lines 25 and 28.

source.note: Must branch on response.status (200 vs 404) before accessing body fields.

reviewLocations.label: searchService.test.ts:5-13 and 32-35 — 3 failing tests
reviewLocations.reason: Three tests assert the old behavior and now fail: status 200 for no-match (line 7), body.results === [] for no-match (line 12), and body.results === [] for blank query (line 34). These need to be rewritten to assert the 404 shape.

source.note: Confirmed failing via test run: 3 failures, all in this file.

reviewLocations.label: searchClient.test.ts:6-9 — false-passing empty-state test
reviewLocations.reason: The empty-state test passes today because it constructs its own { status: 200, body: { results: [] } } fixture manually. But this shape is no longer emitted by the service. Once interpretResponse() is fixed, this fixture must be replaced with a 404-shaped response to test the real path.

source.note: Test passes now but will need updating once interpretResponse() branches on status.

reviewLocations.label: searchService.ts:50-64 — blank query coverage
reviewLocations.reason: The blank-query path (q.length === 0 → results = []) now also returns 404 as a side effect of the shared results.length === 0 branch. It is not mentioned in the PR description. Confirm whether this is intentional.

source.note: Blank query flows into the same 404 branch as a no-match query. May be intentional, but is undocumented.

decisions.question: Is HTTP 404 the right status code for a valid query that returns zero results?
decisions.context: REST conventions differ: 200 + empty list signals the collection exists but nothing matched; 404 signals no resource was found. The compatibility note in docs/sample-context/compatibility.md explicitly flags this as needing team agreement.
decisions.stakes: If 404 is used, all clients must distinguish 'empty results' from genuine errors. Caching layers and proxies may also treat 404 differently from 200, causing unexpected behavior.

sources.note: Explicit open question flagged before implementation.

decisions.question: Is returning 404 for a blank/whitespace query intentional?
decisions.context: The blank-query path previously returned 200 + empty list as a documented special case. The new code returns 404 for blank queries as a side effect — not because they are a 'search miss' but because the shared results.length === 0 branch catches them too.
decisions.stakes: If a caller uses a blank query as an initial 'show nothing' state, it will now receive a 404 and may surface an error to the user instead of an empty state.

sources.note: q.length === 0 path sets results = [] then falls through to the 404 branch.
